citations.title: ELIMINATED: Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini, Nukhba cell commander
citations.excerpt: ELIMINATED: Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini, a Nukhba cell commander in Hamas’ military wing who infiltrated the Re’im Base in Israel during the October 7 Massacre. Recently, he advanced attacks against Israeli civilians & IDF troops and attempted to restore Hamas’ capabilities, in systematic violation of the ceasefire. The terrorist was eliminated in order to remove the threat he posed.

citations.title: COGAT: Israel did not initiate suspension of private-sector goods into Gaza
citations.excerpt: Contrary to recent reports echoed by Hamas, Israel did not initiate the suspension of private-sector operations for the entry of goods into the Gaza Strip. As previously communicated by COGAT, in recent days, private-sector merchants informed COGAT that, due to Hamas’s forced taxation mechanism and threats against merchants who refuse to comply with its demands, they had decided to suspend the coordination of trucks carrying goods into the Gaza Strip until further notice, out of genuine fear for their lives and safety. According to reports received from the merchants, Hamas demands approximately 10,000 NIS for every truck carrying goods into Gaza and requires merchants to sell approximately 30% of their goods in cash, in an effort to gain control over the proceeds. It was also reported that Hamas security personnel arrested the son of one of the merchants and transferred him to Abbas Prison after his father refused to comply with the organization’s taxation demands. This incident, along with the threats and pressure exerted on the merchants, led them to suspend coordination activities out of fear for their lives. It should be emphasized that humanitarian aid continues to enter the Gaza Strip through the UN, international organizations, and donor countries. According to COGAT’s assessments, based on UN reports and evaluations by experts from the international community, the volume of aid entering through these channels is sufficient to adequately meet the needs of the population in Gaza, even without private-sector operations.

citations.title: IDF says Hamas terrorist who attacked Re’im base on Oct. 7 killed in airstrike
citations.excerpt: A Hamas terrorist who took part in the attack on the military’s Re’im base during the October 7 onslaught was killed in an airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip earlier this week, the military announced Friday. The strike on Wednesday killed Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini, the commander of a Nukhba Force cell in Hamas’s military wing, the Israel Defense Forces said. The military said Husseini attacked the Re’im Base on October 7, 2023, and recently was advancing attacks on troops and Israeli civilians, and was attempting to restore Hamas’s capabilities, “in systematic violation of the ceasefire.” Four IDF soldiers were killed and seven wounded during the Hamas-led onslaught while battling terrorists at Re’im, which houses the Gaza Division, the regional unit responsible for the Strip and for protecting southern Israel.

citations.title: Israel cites Gazan merchants angered by Hamas taxes as commercial goods stop entering Strip
citations.excerpt: No commercial goods have entered the Gaza Strip for two days, Israeli authorities said Thursday, blaming the suspension on Gazan merchants angered by taxes imposed by Hamas — a claim that Palestinian importers and the terrorist group denied. The halt to commercial shipments, including fruit and winter clothing, cuts off a key source of food and other critical supplies as fears grow about procuring supplies needed to get through winter in the territory. On Wednesday, COGAT announced the suspension of commercial shipments. Its deputy spokesperson, Lt. Daniel Kantorovich, said the agency was acting on a decision made by Palestinian merchants a day earlier and could reverse it at their behest. “We were prepared to coordinate the entry of their trucks as usual, but the vendors informed us that they were cancelling the coordination due to Hamas’s taxation mechanism and threats against them,” Kantorovich said. In a letter to international representatives involved in implementing the ceasefire, COGAT said merchants reported that Hamas demanded about 10,000 shekels ($3,200) for every truck into Gaza and that traders sell around 30 percent of goods in cash instead of bank transfers.

citations.title: To remove the threat, IDF eliminates Nukhba commander who infiltrated Re’im Base on 10/7
citations.excerpt: Earlier this week (Wednesday), the IDF struck in the southern Gaza Strip and eliminated the terrorist Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini, a Nukhba cell commander in Hamas’ military wing. The terrorist infiltrated the Re’im Base during the October 7th Massacre. Recently, the terrorist advanced attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians and attempted to restore the terrorist organization’s capabilities, in systematic violation of the ceasefire. The terrorist was eliminated in an aerial strike to remove the threat. Prior to the strike, steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance. IDF troops under the Southern Command remain deployed in the area in accordance with the agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat.

passages.text: The IDF continues targeted operations against Hamas operatives involved in the October 7 massacre and subsequent violations of the ceasefire, including the elimination of Nukhba commander Maher Walid Omar al-Husseini who infiltrated Re’im Base.

On Wednesday the IDF struck in southern Gaza eliminating al-Husseini; the announcement came Friday as commercial goods entry was reported halted for days due to merchant suspension over Hamas taxation.
COGAT emphasized that humanitarian aid via UN and international organizations continues and is assessed as sufficient for basic needs even without private-sector commercial goods.

The IDF stated the terrorist was eliminated to remove the threat he posed after advancing attacks and restoring capabilities in systematic violation of the ceasefire, with measures taken to mitigate civilian harm.

COGAT clarified that Israel did not initiate the suspension; merchants stopped coordinating out of fear following Hamas’s forced taxation of about 10,000 NIS per truck, 30% cash requirements, and reported arrests.
Monitor whether commercial coordination resumes and the impact on supply availability ahead of winter, alongside continued IDF operations against ceasefire violators from the October 7 period.
